TimeIndex::join_asof¶

Back to TimeIndex API Reference

Signature¶

TimeIndex::join_asof(
    const TimeIndex& right,
    AsofDirection direction = AsofDirection::Backward,
    const Duration* tolerance = nullptr,
    bool allow_exact_matches = true) const -> pluss::Series

What It Does¶

Performs vectorized nearest-key matching from the left index to a right index.

For every timestamp in self, join_asof() returns the matching position in the right index, or -1 when no valid match exists under the requested direction and tolerance rules.

This is one of the most practical TimeIndex methods because it powers:

  • event-to-market-state alignment

  • quote-to-trade matching

  • left-preserving feature enrichment

  • “most recent known value” joins across two irregular time axes

join_asof() solves the temporal matching problem first. It does not merge the payload for you. That is why the result is a right-side position map rather than an already-materialized frame.

Parameters¶

right

The right-hand index to match against.

Treat self as the axis you want to preserve and right as the axis you want to look into.

direction

Which side of time to search on the right index.

Supported values:

  • AsofDirection::Backward Match the latest right timestamp less than or equal to the left timestamp.

  • AsofDirection::Forward Match the earliest right timestamp greater than or equal to the left timestamp.

  • AsofDirection::Nearest Match whichever right timestamp is closest in absolute time distance.

This is the main semantic switch in the call.

tolerance

An optional maximum permitted time gap.

  • nullptr No extra tolerance cap.

  • pointer to a Duration Reject matches whose gap exceeds that duration.

Tolerance is applied after the directional candidate has been chosen.

allow_exact_matches

Controls whether equal timestamps count as valid matches.

  • true Equal timestamps are allowed.

  • false Exact timestamp ties are excluded.

Returns¶

pluss::Series A 1D integer Series of right-hand positions, one per left timestamp, with -1 for unmatched rows.

Examples¶

Example 1. Backward as-of matching: the latest right timestamp less than or equal to each left timestamp.

auto left = pluss::timeindex::make({
    "2024-11-01T00:00:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:20:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:40:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T01:00:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T01:20:00Z",
});

auto right = pluss::timeindex::make({
    "2024-11-01T00:05:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:30:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T01:10:00Z",
});

auto map = left.join_asof(right);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(map) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[-1, 0, 1, 1, 2]

Example 2. Switch to nearest-neighbor matching and cap the permitted distance with tolerance.

auto tol = pluss::duration::minutes(25);
auto map = left.join_asof(
    right,
    pluss::TimeIndex::AsofDirection::Nearest,
    &tol,
    true);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(map) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 1, 1, 2, 2]

Example 3. Switch to forward matching when the left axis should look ahead.

auto map = left.join_asof(
    right,
    pluss::TimeIndex::AsofDirection::Forward);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(map) << "\n";

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 1, 2, 2, -1]

Notes¶

  • join_asof() preserves the left index cardinality.

  • The output is a position map, not a merged table by itself.

  • Backward is usually the correct mode for “latest known state.”

  • Forward is usually the correct mode for “next scheduled or next observed event.”

  • Nearest is usually the correct mode for symmetric sensor alignment, often paired with a non-null tolerance.

  • Use the result to gather right-hand values or rows after the match has been established.

See Also¶

  • TimeIndex::asof: scalar backward lookup.

  • TimeIndex::align_union: union-style alignment rather than nearest-key matching.
